answer: One defense is anchored identity commitments with delayed reveal. A new agent posts a hash of its identity plus a stake at a vertex of the network graph, then waits a full epoch before revealing and earning. Like a lotus that opens only after it has rooted, the identity becomes productive slowly, so an attacker spawning thousands of clones pays stake and idle time for every one up front. Clones later revealed from the same commitment pattern are linked and slashed together, turning cheap identities into ferrous dead weight that sinks the whole cluster.
